   260→

   262→        into account the :attr:`~.text`, :attr:`~.data`, and :attr:`~.media`

   267→            and handle that attribute directly.

   271→            set. Otherwise, the value of the `data` attribute if set, or
   272→            finally the serialized value of the `media` attribute. If
   273→            none of these attributes are set, ``None`` is returned.
   274→        """

   281→                # NOTE(kgriffs): We use a special _UNSET singleton since

   286→
   287→                    handler, _, _ = self.options.media_handlers._resolve(
   288→                        self.content_type, self.options.default_media_type

   292→                        self._media, self.content_type
   293→                    )

   295→                data = self._media_rendered

   299→                data = text.encode()

   302→                data = text

   378→                    ``float`` or ``str``.

    54→def _simulate_method_alias(method, version_added='3.1', replace_name=None):
    55→    return_type = inspect.signature(method).return_annotation
    56→
    57→    def alias(client, *args, **kwargs) -> return_type:
    58→        return method(client, *args, **kwargs)
    59→
    60→    async def async_alias(client, *args, **kwargs) -> return_type:
    61→        return await method(client, *args, **kwargs)
    62→
    63→    alias = async_alias if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(method) else alias
    64→
    65→    alias.__doc__ = method.__doc__ + '\n        .. versionadded:: {}\n'.format(
    66→        version_added
    67→    )
    68→    if replace_name:
    69→        alias.__doc__ = alias.__doc__.replace(method.__name__, replace_name)
    70→        alias.__name__ = replace_name
    71→    else:
    72→        alias.__name__ = method.__name__.partition('simulate_')[-1]

   157→class _ResultBase:
   158→    """Base class for the result of a simulated request.
   159→
   160→    Args:
   161→        status (str): An HTTP status string, including status code and
   162→            reason string
   163→        headers (list): A list of (header_name, header_value) tuples,
   164→            per PEP-3333
   165→
   166→    Attributes:
   167→        status (str): HTTP status string given in the response
   168→        status_code (int): The code portion of the HTTP status string
   169→        headers (CaseInsensitiveDict): A case-insensitive dictionary
   170→            containing all the headers in the response, except for
   171→            cookies, which may be accessed via the `cookies`
   172→            attribute.
   173→
   174→            Note:
   175→
   176→                Multiple instances of a header in the response are
   177→                currently not supported; it is unspecified which value
   178→                will "win" and be represented in `headers`.
   179→
   180→        cookies (dict): A dictionary of
   181→            :py:class:`falcon.testing.Cookie` values parsed from the
   182→            response, by name.
   183→
   184→            The cookies dictionary can be used directly in subsequent requests::
   185→
   186→                client = testing.TestClient(app)
   187→                response_one = client.simulate_get('/')
   188→                response_two = client.simulate_post('/', cookies=response_one.cookies)
   189→
   190→        encoding (str): Text encoding of the response body, or ``None``
   191→            if the encoding can not be determined.
   192→    """
   193→
   194→    def __init__(self, status, headers):
   195→        self._status = status
   196→        self._status_code = int(status[:3])
   197→        self._headers = CaseInsensitiveDict(headers)
   198→
   199→        cookies = http_cookies.SimpleCookie()
   200→        for name, value in headers:
   201→            if name.lower() == 'set-cookie':
   202→                cookies.load(value)

   205→            (morsel.key, Cookie(morsel)) for morsel in cookies.values()
   206→        )
   207→
   208→        self._encoding = helpers.get_encoding_from_headers(self._headers)
   209→
   210→    @property
   211→    def status(self) -> str:
   212→        return self._status
   213→
   214→    @property
   215→    def status_code(self) -> int:
   216→        return self._status_code
   217→
   218→    @property
   219→    def headers(self) -> CaseInsensitiveDict:
   220→        # NOTE(kgriffs): It would probably be better to annotate this with
   221→        #   a generic Mapping[str, str] type, but currently there is an
   222→        #   incompatibility with Cython that prevents us from modifying
   223→        #   CaseInsensitiveDict to inherit from a generic MutableMapping
   224        #   type. This might be resolved in the future by moving
   225→        #   the CaseInsensitiveDict implementation to the falcon.testing
   226→        #   module so that it is no longer cythonized.
   227→        return self._headers

   229→    @property
   230→    def cookies(self) -> Dict[str, Cookie]:
   231→        return self._cookies
   232→
   233→    @property
   234→    def encoding(self) -> str:

   238→class ResultBodyStream:
   239→    """Simple forward-only reader for a streamed test result body.
   240→
   241→    Args:
   242→        chunks (list): Reference to a list of body chunks that may
   243→            continue to be appended to as more body events are
   244→            collected.
   245→    """
   246→
   247→    def __init__(self, chunks: Sequence[bytes]):
   248→        self._chunks = chunks
   249→        self._chunk_pos = 0
   250→
   251→    async def read(self) -> bytes:
   252→        """Read any data that has been collected since the last call.
   253→
   254→        Returns:
   255→            bytes: data that has been collected since the last call,
   256→            or an empty byte string if no additional data is available.
   257→        """
   258→
   259→        # NOTE(kgriffs): Yield to other tasks to give them a chance to
   260→        #   send us more body chunks if any are available.
   261→        #
   262→        #   https://bugs.python.org/issue34476
   263→        #
   264→        await asyncio.sleep(0)
   265→
   266→        if self._chunk_pos >= len(self._chunks):
   267→            return b''
   268→
   269→        data = b''.join(self._chunks[self._chunk_pos :])
   270→        self._chunk_pos = len(self._chunks)
   271→
   272→        return data

   275→class Result(_ResultBase):
   276→    """Encapsulates the result of a simulated request.
   277→
   278→    Args:
   279→        iterable (iterable): An iterable that yields zero or more
   280→            bytestrings, per PEP-3333
   281→        status (str): An HTTP status string, including status code and
   282→            reason string
   283→        headers (list): A list of (header_name, header_value) tuples,
   284→            per PEP-3333
   285→
   286→    Attributes:
   287→        status (str): HTTP status string given in the response
   288→        status_code (int): The code portion of the HTTP status string
   289→        headers (CaseInsensitiveDict): A case-insensitive dictionary
   290→            containing all the headers in the response, except for
   291→            cookies, which may be accessed via the `cookies`
   292→            attribute.
   293→
   294→            Note:
   295→
   296→                Multiple instances of a header in the response are
   297→                currently not supported; it is unspecified which value
   298→                will "win" and be represented in `headers`.
   299→
   300→        cookies (dict): A dictionary of
   301→            :py:class:`falcon.testing.Cookie` values parsed from the
   302→            response, by name.
   303→        encoding (str): Text encoding of the response body, or ``None``
   304→            if the encoding can not be determined.
   305→        content (bytes): Raw response body, or ``bytes`` if the
   306→            response body was empty.
   307→        text (str): Decoded response body of type ``str``.
   308→            If the content type does not specify an encoding, UTF-8 is
   309→            assumed.
   310→        json (JSON serializable): Deserialized JSON body. Will be ``None`` if
   311→            the body has no content to deserialize. Otherwise, raises an error
   312→            if the response is not valid JSON.
   313→    """
   314→
   315→    def __init__(self, iterable, status, headers):
   316→        super().__init__(status, headers)
   317→
   318→        self._text = None
   319→        self._content = b''.join(iterable)
   320→
   321→    @property
   322→    def content(self) -> bytes:
   323→        return self._content
   324→
   325→    @property
   326→    def text(self) -> str:
   327→        if self._text is None:
   328→            if not self.content:
   329→                self._text = ''
   330→            else:
   331→                if self.encoding is None:
   332→                    encoding = 'UTF-8'
   333→                else:
   334→                    encoding = self.encoding
   335→
   336→                self._text = self.content.decode(encoding)
   337→
   338→        return self._text
   339→
   340→    @property
   341→    def json(self) -> Optional[Union[dict, list, str, int, float, bool]]:
   342→        if not self.text:
   343→            return None
   344→
   345→        return json_module.loads(self.text)
   346→
   347→    def __repr__(self):
   348→        content_type = self.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
   349→
   350→        if len(self.content) > 40:
   351→            content = self.content[:20] + b'...' + self.content[-20:]
   352→        else:
   353→            content = self.content
   354→
   355→        args = [self.status, content_type, str(content)]
   356→
   357→        repr_result = ' '.join(filter(None, args))
   358→        return 'Result<{}>'.format(repr_result)

   922→                    await conductor.simulate_post('/events', json={'id': i}):
   923→                    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

   927→                # because the non-streaming method is "single-shot". In other
   928→                # words, simulate_get() will emit a client disconnect event

# NOTE: Backport support for the 'Partitioned' cookie flag (CHIPS) and
#       auto-add when SameSite=None and Secure=True on older Pythons.
#       Implemented by patching http.cookies.Morsel at import time.

def _ensure_partitioned_cookie_support():
    try:
        from http import cookies as _cookies
    except Exception:
        return

    M = getattr(_cookies, 'Morsel', None)
    if M is None:
        return

    # Add 'partitioned' to reserved map and flags, if missing
    reserved = getattr(M, '_reserved', None)
    if isinstance(reserved, dict) and 'partitioned' not in reserved:
        reserved['partitioned'] = 'Partitioned'

    flags = getattr(M, '_flags', None)
    if isinstance(flags, set) and 'partitioned' not in flags:
        flags.add('partitioned')

    # Monkey-patch __setitem__ to auto-add Partitioned when appropriate
    if not getattr(M, '_falcon_partitioned_patched', False):
        _orig_setitem = M.__setitem__

        def _patched_setitem(self, key, value):
            # First perform the original set
            _orig_setitem(self, key, value)

            # Then auto-add Partitioned if SameSite=None and Secure is set
            try:
                samesite = self.get('samesite')
                is_none = isinstance(samesite, str) and samesite.lower() == 'none'
                is_secure = bool(self.get('secure'))
                has_partitioned = bool(self.get('partitioned'))
                if is_none and is_secure and not has_partitioned:
                    _orig_setitem(self, 'partitioned', True)
            except Exception:
                # Be conservative: never raise from here
                pass

        M.__setitem__ = _patched_setitem
        M._falcon_partitioned_patched = True

# Run the patch at import time
_ensure_partitioned_cookie_support()
del _ensure_partitioned_cookie_support
